sources.citation: Bickford, J. Albert. 2005. The Signed Languages of Eastern Europe. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2005-026. Dallas: SIL International / University of North Dakota. 37 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The report is a wordlist (lexicostatistical) comparison plus sociolinguistic notes; section 3.8 'Moldova' (pp. 11-12) covers Soviet-era deaf education, Russian/Romanian SL influence, fingerspelling 'in Romanian' vs 'in Russian', high lexical similarity to Russian SL, and says no dictionary or interpreter-training programme was found. A a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for stress/prosod/accent/phonolog/suprasegment hits only one bibliography entry (Marentette & Mayberry 2000, not about Moldova).

sources.note: No descriptive reference for vsi. Of the 11 refs, only Bickford 2005 concerns Moldova; the other ten (Mahoney 2018 MA thesis on Estonian/Latvian SL handshape aperture; Kagirov et al. 2019 Russian SL; Power 2020 diss. and 2023 chapter on Russian-Tajik SL; Abdel-Fattah 2016 SAGE encyclopedia; Hollman 2016 Estonian SL; Pfau et al. 2022 Georgian SL negation; Danielius 2004 Lithuanian SL sketch; Geer 2011 Mongolian SL kinship; Ethnologue 2025) carry language code fields for other sign languages and are attached to the whole Eastern-European SL group. Records saved as glottolog_ref_<id>.html.
Nothing on phonology or stress; the English article cites only Bickford 2005; Wikidata cites only Ethnologue. Romanian Wikipedia page does not exist (404).
